newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF's Ogawa says Japan surplus on shrinking trend.
newsitem.headline: MOF's Ogawa says Japan surplus on shrinking trend.

text.p: Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa said on Monday he thinks Japan's current account surplus has been shrinking and, despite some monthly fluctuations, the trend is likely to stay that way.
"The general trend is that the ratio of the current account surplus to gross domestic product is drastically falling. I think this general trend has been established," Ogawa told a news conference.

He was responding to questions about comments made by U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers on Friday when he warned Japan against trying to export its way out of its economic woes. Summers also urged Japan to restore domestic demand-led growth and repair its financial system.

Asked whether calls for additional fiscal stimulus measures would grow louder given the sluggish domestic demand, Ogawa said he expected Japan to be able to achieve its economic growth forecast of 1.9 percent in 1997/98, with the passage of next fiscal year's budget.
He reiterated his view that it would not be right to raise taxes for fiscal consolidation if the government did not reduce its spending first.
